title: HIF-1alpha/BNIP3L-mediated mitophagy is involved in T-2 toxin-induced myocardial injury.
authors: Li, Qian; Wang, Miao; Zuo, Juan; Dong, Zaichao; Sha, Tongtong; Luo, Kangting; Zhang, Huanxia; Dou, Yanjie; Zhou, Guoyu; Ba, Yue; Yu, Fang-Fang
one_liner_zh: 该文研究T-2毒素通过HIF-1alpha/BNIP3L介导线粒体自噬导致心肌损伤，仅涉及蛋白-蛋白互作（BNIP3L-LC3）和分子对接，无蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: T-2 toxin, the most toxic type A mycotoxin, induces cardiotoxicity and impairs cardiac function. Herein, we investigated the regulatory role of mitophagy in T-2 toxin-induced myocardial injury. Using the Comparative Toxicogenomics Database, we identified 288 rat genes associated with T-2 toxin-induced myocardial injury. Gene Ontology and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes enrichment analyses revealed that mitophagy was significantly associated with myocardial injury. Protein-protein interaction network analysis revealed HIF-1alpha as the core regulatory gene. Rats were exposed to T-2 toxin and assigned to control, low-dose (100 ng/g.bw/day), and high-dose (200 ng/g.bw/day) groups. H9C2 cardiomyocytes were divided into control, low-dose (3 ng/mL), medium-dose (6 ng/mL), and high-dose (12 ng/mL) groups. High-dose T-2 toxin exposure caused significant myocardial damage, increased lactate dehydrogenase and creatine kinase-myocardial band levels, elevated reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, and upregulated HIF-1alpha expression in the nucleus. Flow cytometry showed that T-2 toxin significantly decreased mitochondrial membrane potential. Transmission electron microscopy revealed mitochondrial swelling, vacuolation, and cristae disruption. Molecular docking and immunofluorescence confirmed direct binding between BNIP3L and LC3. T-2 toxin significantly upregulated HIF-1alpha, BNIP3L, and LC3 mRNA and protein levels, promoted LC3-I to LC3-II conversion, and suppressed P62 expression in tissues and cells. Immunohistochemistry further confirmed these protein expression trends. Myocardial injury was ameliorated by 2-ME2 by suppressing HIF-1alpha accumulation and BNIP3L-mediated mitophagy. In summary, T-2 toxin-induced ROS accumulation activated HIF-1alpha in cardiomyocytes, which regulated BNIP3L-LC3 binding, mediated mitophagy, and ultimately caused myocardial injury.
abstract_zh: T-2毒素，作为毒性最强的A型单端孢霉烯族毒素，可诱导心脏毒性并损害心脏功能。在此，我们研究了线粒体自噬在T-2毒素诱导心肌损伤中的调控作用。利用比较毒物基因组学数据库，我们鉴定了288个大鼠基因与T-2毒素诱导的心肌损伤相关。基因本体论和京都基因与基因组百科全书富集分析显示，线粒体自噬与心肌损伤显著相关。蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用网络分析揭示HIF-1α为核心调控基因。大鼠暴露于T-2毒素，并分为对照组、低剂量组（100 ng/g.bw/天）和高剂量组（200 ng/g.bw/天）。H9C2心肌细胞分为对照组、低剂量组（3 ng/mL）、中剂量组（6 ng/mL）和高剂量组（12 ng/mL）。高剂量T-2毒素暴露导致显著心肌损伤，增加乳酸脱氢酶和肌酸激酶心肌带水平，升高活性氧（ROS）积累，并上调细胞核中HIF-1α表达。流式细胞术显示，T-2毒素显著降低线粒体膜电位。透射电子显微镜显示线粒体肿胀、空泡化和嵴断裂。分子对接和免疫荧光确认BNIP3L与LC3直接结合。T-2毒素显著上调HIF-1α、BNIP3L和LC3的mRNA和蛋白水平，促进LC3-I向LC3-II转化，并抑制组织和细胞中P62表达。免疫组织化学进一步证实了这些蛋白表达趋势。通过2-ME2抑制HIF-1α积累和BNIP3L介导的线粒体自噬，心肌损伤得到改善。总之，T-2毒素诱导的ROS积累激活了心肌细胞中的HIF-1α，其调控BNIP3L-LC3结合，介导线粒体自噬，最终导致心肌损伤。
